page.layout: One printed page, title page with a woodcut border; the title block is centred inside the border; a printer's device (eagle with snakes on a globe) sits in the centre below the title, with the mottoes set vertically on either side; the imprint and date are centred at the foot of the block. No running text, no margins.
page.notes: The title is printed in large spaced capitals with the word "PROMTVARII" (sic, for Promptuarii) and the first line set in larger type. The mottoes "IN VIRTVTE," and "ET FORTVNA." are printed vertically on the left and right of the device; they are read here in the order top-to-bottom, left then right. The date line shows "1578" with the digit 7 partly obscured by a stain; the reading 1578 is taken from the printed date and the faint ghost figure at the right of the date is show-through and is left out. The mark "A`" in the second block reproduces the printed accent-like sign after A. Stains and tears at the foot of the page are damage, not text. The woodcut device itself is not text and is not transcribed. Doubtful: "tissimis" in the line "tissimis autoribus" appears to have a missing "s" or ligature at the start of the word; read as printed. "successerunt" is partly obscured by a crease; the reading is the most likely one.
